q: 1. If Ix = M.O.I. about x-axis and Iy = M.O.I. about y-axis, then moment of inertia about z-axis is given by
explain: This is the Perpendicular Axis Theorem, applicable to planar bodies where the Z-axis is perpendicular to the X-Y plane.

q: 2. When equal and opposite forces applied to a body, tend to elongate it, the stress so produced, is called
explain: Tensile stress is the internal resistance developed when external 'pull' forces act to increase the length of a body.

q: 3. Modulus of rigidity may be defined as the ratio of
explain: Modulus of Rigidity (G or C) is the ratio of shear stress to shear strain, representing the material's resistance to shearing deformation.

q: 4. Two bars of different materials and same size are subjected to same tensile force. If the bars have unit elongation in the ratio of 2:5, then the ratio of modulus of elasticity of the two materials will be
explain: Since $\delta l = Pl/AE$, and P, l, A are constant, $E$ is inversely proportional to elongation. Thus, $E_1/E_2 = \delta l_2/\delta l_1 = 5/2$.

q: 5. The length of a conical bar is l, density w and modulus of elasticity E. The elongation of the bar under the action of its own weight will be
explain: As derived in mechanics, the self-weight elongation of a cone is $\frac{wl^2}{6E}$.

q: 6. Strain rosters are used to
explain: Strain rosettes are a combination of three or more strain gauges used to measure the linear strains in different directions on a surface to determine the state of strain at a point.

q: 7. A rod is enclosed centrally in a tube and the assembly is subjected to a compressive load, then
options: both rod and tube are under compression
tube is under tension and rod is under compression
explain: In a composite assembly subjected to an external compressive load, both components must compress together to maintain compatibility of displacement.

q: 8. A steel bar 5 m long and 40 mm wide is heated from 15°C to 40°C and it is free to expand. The bar will induce
explain: If a material is free to expand or contract during a temperature change without any restraint, no internal resistance (stress) is developed.

q: 9. A bar of copper and steel form a composite system, which is heated to a temperature of 40°C. The stress induced in the copper bar will be
explain: Copper has a higher coefficient of thermal expansion than steel. When heated, copper wants to expand more but is restricted by the steel, putting copper into compression and steel into tension.

q: 10. The thermal or temperature stress is a function of
explain: Thermal stress is calculated using the formula σ = αtE, where α is the coefficient of linear expansion, t is the temperature change, and E is the Modulus of Elasticity.

q: 11. The ratio of change in volume to the original volume is called
explain: Volumetric strain (εv) is the change in volume (dV) divided by the original volume (V).

q: 12. The volumetric strain is the ratio of the
options: original thickness to the change in thickness
change in thickness to the original thickness
original volume to the change in volume
change in volume to the original volume
explain: Volumetric strain measures the overall deformation of a body in terms of volume change relative to its initial state.

q: 13. Young's Modulus is the ratio of the normal stress to the
explain: By definition, Young's Modulus is the constant of proportionality between normal stress and normal strain within the limit of proportionality.

q: 14. A tie is a member which
options: is subjected to axial tension primarily
explain: In structural engineering, a 'tie' is a tension member designed to resist forces that pull it apart.

q: 15. When a rectangular beam is loaded transversely, the maximum tensile stress is developed on the
explain: For a simply supported beam under downward loads, the beam sags. This creates compression in the top fibers and tension in the bottom fibers.

q: 16. When a body is subjected to a direct tensile stress (σ) in one plane, the maximum shear stress is ............ the maximum normal stress.
explain: Maximum normal stress is σ (at 0°), and maximum shear stress is σ/2 (at 45°). Therefore, max shear is half of max normal stress.

q: 17. The capacity of a strained body for doing work on the removal of the straining force, is called
explain: This is another definition of resilience, emphasizing the ability to return to the original state and release stored energy.

q: 18. When a member is subjected to a twisting moment, the material will be subjected to ............
explain: Torsion creates internal resistance in the form of shear stresses that act on the cross-sectional planes and longitudinal planes.

q: 19. In a shaft subjected to pure torsion, maximum shear stress will occur at ............
options: a distance of semi-radius from centre
explain: Since shear stress is proportional to the radius ($r$), it is zero at the center and reaches its maximum value at the outer boundary (periphery) where $r=R$.

q: 20. The proportional limit of mild steel specimen is taken as the stress corresponding to a permanent set of ............
explain: While proof stress is often 0.2%, the limit of proportionality is very sensitive and is often associated with a very small permanent set like 0.01%.

q: 21. Strain energy due to bending stress is ............
explain: For a beam subjected to a bending moment $M$, the total strain energy is obtained by integrating $\frac{M^2}{2EI}$ over the length of the beam.

q: 22. The intensity of direct longitudinal stress in the cross-section at any point distant r from the neutral axis, is proportional to ............
explain: According to the bending equation (M/I = σ/y), the bending stress (σ) is directly proportional to the distance (y or r) from the neutral axis.

q: 23. A tensile test is performed on a mild steel round bar. Its diameter after fracture will ............
explain: Mild steel is ductile; before it breaks, it undergoes 'necking,' which is a localized reduction in the cross-sectional area.

q: 24. A member with a cross section of a mm² is subjected to a force of P N. It is L mm long and of Young's Modulus, E N/mm². The strain will be
explain: Strain = stress/E = (P/A)/E = P/AE, a dimensionless ratio (mm/mm).

q: 25. If α is the coefficient of linear expansion, T is the rise in temperature then thermal stress is given by
explain: Thermal stress (fully restrained) = E·α·T.

q: 26. Stress in a beam due to simple bending, is
explain: Bending stress varies linearly (directly proportional) with distance from the neutral axis, σ = My/I.

q: 27. If a material has identical properties in all directions, it is said to be
explain: Isotropic means direction-independent material properties.

q: 28. A visco elastic material
explain: Viscoelastic materials exhibit both viscous and elastic behavior, meaning their stress-strain response depends on time/rate.

q: 29. A brittle material will
explain: Brittle materials fracture suddenly with little to no prior warning (no significant plastic deformation).

q: 30. The moment of inertia of a square section is given by
explain: For a square of side b, I = b⁴/12 (special case of bd³/12 with b=d).

q: 31. The moment of inertia of triangular section b×h about the base is
explain: Standard formula: I_base = bh³/12 for a triangle of base b and height h.

q: 32. Centrifugal force is given by
explain: Centrifugal acceleration/specific force = v²/R (per unit mass form used in this option set).

q: 33. The maximum number of transverse shear forces possible at one end of an element of a plane truss are
explain: Truss members carry only axial force (two-force members) — no transverse shear develops at the ends.

q: 34. The safe value of stress below which the material will not fail when subjected to reversal of stress is known as
explain: The endurance limit is the stress amplitude below which a material can withstand infinite stress reversals.

q: 35. The bending moment acting on the plane of an element will cause the following type of stress on the plane
explain: Bending moment produces normal (bending) stress that varies linearly across the section — tension on one side, compression on the other.

q: 36. As the elastic limit reaches, tensile strain
options: decreases in proportion to the stress
increases in proportion to the stress
explain: As per the answer key for this set; near the elastic limit the linear stress–strain proportionality begins to break down.

q: 37. When a rectangular beam is loaded transversely the maximum compressive stress is developed on the:
explain: For a typical sagging beam, the top fiber experiences maximum compressive stress.

q: 38. Stress may be defined as force per unit:
explain: Stress = Force / Area, by definition.
